status.label: Out
status.shortComment: Barkley (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's contest against the Jaguars in London.
status.longComment: Barkley didn't practice this week in the wake of suffering a right hamstring injury this past Sunday against the Rams, so his lack of availability for Week 5 doesn't come as a surprise. With Tank Bigsby (abdomen) on injured reserve, it'll be the Will Shipley show out of the Eagles backfield Sunday, while Dameon Pierce also is on hand for RB reps that linger, and Jaydon Blue and Carson Steele are options to be elevated from the practice squad. Barkley's next chance for game action is Sunday, Oct. 18 versus the Panthers.

status.label: Injured Reserve
status.shortComment: The Eagles placed Bigsby (abdomen) on injured reserve Tuesday, Zach Berman of The Athletic reports.
status.longComment: Bigsby will undergo core muscle surgery for an abdominal injury that he picked up during the Eagles' Week 4 loss to the Rams. The fourth-year pro will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 9 against the Giants. Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is also considered week-to-week, so with Bigsby on IR, Will Shipley could be the Eagles' starting running back for Week 5 against the Jaguars on Sunday in London.

status.label: Out
status.shortComment: Smith (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's contest versus the Jaguars in London.
status.longComment: Smith was seen running on a side field Thursday before getting in some rehab work Friday, but he was listed as a non-participant on all three of the Eagles' Week 5 injury reports due to a lingering hamstring issue and thus won't play Sunday. With Hollywood Brown (ankle) also sidelined this weekend, Philadelphia's options at wide receiver will be Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Elijah Moore and Britain Covey.

status.label: Out
status.shortComment: Brown (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
status.longComment: An ankle injury will cause Brown to miss a third consecutive game, and his next chance to play is Week 6 against the Panthers on Sunday, Oct. 18. DeVonta Smith (hamstring) has already been ruled out, so Philadelphia's top wideouts against Jacksonville will be Dontayvion Wicks, rookie Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper, with Elijah Moore and Britain Covey also providing depth at the position.

status.label: Out
status.shortComment: Kendall (knee) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
status.longComment: With Cam Jurgens (concussion) being traded to the Ravens, Kendall was set to be the Eagles' starting center for Week 5. The second-year offensive lineman will need to wait another week to take over for Jurgens, leaving Jake Majors as the starter for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.

status.label: Questionable
status.shortComment: Greenard (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against Jacksonville.
status.longComment: Greenard was held out of practice all week due to an ankle injury he sustained against the Rams in Week 4. Despite the lack of practice, the Eagles are still keeping the door open for Greenard to play Sunday, but if he's not cleared to suit up, then Jalyx Hunt, Arnold Ebiketie and A.J. Epenesa would all be in line for more defensive snaps.

status.label: Out
status.shortComment: Epps (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
status.longComment: Epps will miss a second consecutive game due to a groin injury. His next chance to play is Week 6 against the Panthers on Sunday, Oct. 18, though he would need to practice in at least a limited capacity to have a realistic shot at returning against Carolina. Michael Carter should once again start next to Andrew Mukuba at safety in Epps' absence.
